verdict_reason: The max-factoring fix in `_weight_matrix_stats` is correct and I could not break it anywhere in the representable float32 range. Stable rank is a ratio of squared norms and therefore exactly scale-invariant; on `diag(10..1)/10`, whose exact stable rank is 3.85, the helper returns 3.849999320273355 at 1e-30 and 3.850000255895395 at 1e-25, 1e-13, 1, 1e13, 1e25 and 2.406159650500376e38 -- the claimed 3.85 reproduces to rel 2.4e-07 at worst, against the pre-fix 0.0 at 1e-25 and 10.0 at 1e30. End-to-end through the REAL `evaluate()` on gpt2 with every parameter multiplied by a constant: mean_stable_rank_normalized = 0.059512118305295986 / 0.059512118678535286 / 0.059512126070062614 at scales 1e-37 / 1 / 1.894e37 (the largest scale at which gpt2's max weight 17.4193172454834 is still representable, giving a top weight of 3.30e38), i.e. rel <= 1.3e-07; _meta_mean_stable_rank 45.70530685846732 / 45.70530714511511 / 45.70531282180809 and norm_uniformity 0.8920787568898595 / 0.8920787470035918 / 0.8920787576851452 over the same range. The scale-covariant outputs track exactly: mean_frobenius_norm 1.6499584889006456e-35 / 164.99584980827348 / 3.1257615081751625e+39.
comparable_reason: The raw norms are architecture-conditioned and the file says so: ||W||_F grows as sqrt(mn) and stable rank is bounded by min(m,n), which is why `_meta_mean_stable_rank` (rho +0.830 with d_model per the file's own record) is demoted and `mean_stable_rank_normalized` -- stable rank divided by its own bound min(m,n), hence in [0,1] -- is the promoted feature. That normalization is dimensionally sound and I verified it is scale-exact. `norm_uniformity` = max(0, 1-CV) over layers is likewise scale-free and measured invariant to 1.2e-08. The caveat is that dividing by min(m,n) removes the SHAPE term but not any width-dependent initialisation scale, which is exactly why `_meta_mean_rms_weight_scale` was demoted alongside.
github_reason: Stable rank ||W||_F^2/||W||_2^2 is a textbook quantity (Rudelson & Vershynin 2007; Tropp 2015 Sec. 7) with no single released reference implementation to fetch. I verified it instead against an exact analytic anchor: diag(10..1)/10 has stable rank sum(i^2)/100 / (1) = 3.85 exactly, reproduced to 3.850000255895395 (rel 6.6e-08) at six of seven probe scales and 3.849999320273355 (rel 2.4e-07) at 1e-30.
paper_reason: No source paper publishes a per-layer weight-norm profile for a specific released checkpoint that this task should reproduce; the analytic anchor above is the appropriate check and it passes.
confounds_reason: The file records rho +0.830 with d_model for `_meta_mean_stable_rank` and rho -0.582 (fitting d^-0.471, essentially the 1/sqrt(d) fan-in init prescribes) for `_meta_mean_rms_weight_scale`; both are demoted for that reason. The promoted `mean_stable_rank_normalized` divides out the min(m,n) bound, which removes the mechanical shape term. I did not re-measure these correlations over the archive.
defects: SILENT PARTIAL FAILURE WITH NO COUNTER: a single non-finite weight entry is absorbed without any signal. Injecting one NaN into gpt2's transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.weight moved mean_stable_rank_normalized 0.059512118678535286 -> 0.05922291232738486 (-0.49%) and mean_frobenius_norm 164.99584980827348 -> 162.69454354985376 (-1.4%), while the output dict contains no key matching /fail|nan/ and _meta_n_layers still reads 12. The module docstring says NaN rows are 'excluded by the nan-aware aggregation', which is a defensible policy, but a reader cannot tell that exclusion happened.

INCONSISTENT NaN POLICY BETWEEN THE TWO STABLE-RANK AGGREGATES: `_meta_mean_stable_rank` is `np.array(srank_per_layer).mean()` (NaN-propagating) while `mean_stable_rank_normalized` is `np.nanmean(...)` (NaN-dropping). When whole layers fail they disagree: with gpt2's weights multiplied by 2.406159650500376e38 (which overflows the largest weights to inf), `_meta_mean_stable_rank` and norm_uniformity are both NaN while mean_stable_rank_normalized returns a finite 0.09074918869967274 against a true 0.059512118678535286 -- +52.5%, silently finite. Same quantity, two aggregation conventions, one of which hides the failure.

TEST COVERAGE: the discovery-based forward-hook leak suite does not cover this task at all (it registers no hook, so the exclusion is honest), and there is no regression pinning the scale ladder that the fix was written for -- the 3.85 anchor lives only in a source comment.
fix: Nothing is required for GREEN; the invariance claim reproduces. Emit a `_meta_n_failed_weight_matrices` counter so a partially-failed model is visible, and make the two stable-rank aggregates use the same NaN convention (prefer nanmean in both, with the counter carrying the failure signal) so they cannot disagree by 52.5% on the same input.
